claims.text: EF Core docs: dotnet ef migrations add <Name> compares the model against a snapshot of it as of the last migration, and generates a migration source file trackable in source control; dotnet ef database update applies pending migrations.

EF Core docs: calling context.Database.Migrate() (or MigrateAsync()) applies migrations programmatically at runtime, the same effect as dotnet ef database update; a typical ASP.NET Core app calls it once during startup.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, entity-framework/core/managing-schemas/migrations/applying.md, "Apply migrations at runtime"

claims.text: EF Core docs: applied migrations are recorded in a history table, __EFMigrationsHistory by default; manually inserting one row (MigrationId, ProductVersion) to mark a migration applied without running it is a technique the docs themselves describe.
claims.source_hint: EF Core docs, entity-framework/core/managing-schemas/migrations/managing.md "Resetting all migrations"; history-table.md

claims.text: MigrationBaseline.ApplyIfNeeded returns early if __EFMigrationsHistory exists, or if customers does not; otherwise it creates __EFMigrationsHistory itself and inserts one row for 20260923154631_InitialCreate / 10.0.4, then returns without running any migration.

Program.cs calls MigrationBaseline.ApplyIfNeeded(context) immediately before context.Database.Migrate(), once, inside a service scope created right after the app is built and before any middleware runs.

AddPasswordHashToCustomers.Up adds a nullable password_hash text column to customers via AddColumn, then runs one raw-SQL UPDATE backfilling all 5 seeded customers with the same password hash; Down drops the column.

Live run against stage-1: __EFMigrationsHistory has exactly 3 rows, MigrationId InitialCreate/AddPasswordHashToCustomers/AddOrderCustomerNavigation, in order — one per migration .cs file, not per file in Migrations/ (7 total).
claims.source_hint: live: docker exec donhang-db psql -U donhang -d donhang -c 'select "MigrationId" from "__EFMigrationsHistory"...'

claims.text: On a database whose tables came from db/schema.sql but whose __EFMigrationsHistory is empty, Migrate() runs InitialCreate's CreateTable calls and fails with a 'relation already exists' error.
claims.source_hint: InitialCreate.cs:15-92; live: CREATE TABLE customers (id integer); on stage-1 lab db -> 'ERROR: relation "customers" already exists'
